name: humanizer
description: Agent skill that removes signs of AI-generated writing from text
one_liner: A free tool that rewrites AI-generated text so it reads like a real person wrote it, without changing the facts, by fixing 35 known 'tells' of AI writing (like overused words and fake-sounding lists).
buyer: A content marketer, student, or freelance writer who uses AI to draft content but needs the final version to pass as human-written for a client, professor, or platform that penalizes obvious AI text.
business_use_cases: A content agency runs every AI-drafted blog post through it before client delivery, since clients increasingly reject copy that 'sounds like ChatGPT.'
A student or professional uses it to clean up AI-assisted cover letters and essays so they read naturally in their own voice.
A social media manager humanizes AI-drafted captions and newsletters so brand voice stays consistent and doesn't feel robotic.

money_ideas.idea: Wrap it as a simple paid web app (paste text, get humanized text back) charging per word or per month, targeting freelancers and students directly.
Sell it as a Chrome extension that humanizes text inline inside Google Docs or ChatGPT, priced as a one-time purchase or small monthly fee.

steal_this: Ship a bare-bones 'paste your AI text, get it humanized' website this weekend with a free tier (500 words) and a $9/month unlimited tier — this is a well-understood, high-demand niche with clear willingness to pay.
